system.name: Fat-Tree QRAM
system.one_liner: a quantum random access memory architecture that pipelines O(log N) queries in O(log N) time using O(N) qubits

content.subject: the gate-level schedule of address-loading, memory-access, and unloading operations for three pipelined Fat-Tree QRAM queries

elements.name: L (load)
elements.role: loads one address qubit's (or the bus's) routing information into a tree level before descending further

elements.name: S (store)
elements.role: stores/commits an address qubit's rotation at a router of that level

elements.name: R (rotate)
elements.role: applies the controlled rotation that steers the query along one address qubit at that level

elements.name: T (two-qubit gate)
elements.role: a two-qubit gate that propagates the query state one tree level deeper toward memory

elements.name: S-I
elements.role: local swap of even-indexed routers between adjacent QRAM sizes, run once per pipeline interval

elements.name: S-II
elements.role: local swap of odd-indexed routers between adjacent QRAM sizes, run once per pipeline interval

elements.name: CG
elements.role: the controlled gate at the tree's deepest level where the query actually reads the memory cell

elements.name: primed operations (L', S', R', T')
elements.role: mirror of the unprimed operations, undoing the routing as the query and its result ascend back out of the tree

elements.name: level band
elements.role: a colour-coded row band (green/orange/pink) matching one level of the QRAM tree at left

elements.name: QRAM tree
elements.role: the small reference diagram keying each colour to a level of the fat-tree QRAM being scheduled

relations.what: a loaded address qubit is rotated at the same level in a later cycle
the rotated qubit drives a two-qubit gate that propagates the query one level deeper
successive levels' gates carry the query down to the controlled gate at the memory cell
after the memory access, the same levels are retraced outward via mirrored primed operations
even- and odd-indexed local swaps alternate every pipeline interval to shift each query along the tree
the tree's dashed tiers are keyed by colour to the grid's row bands

values.what: the operation mnemonics filling each grid cell (L1, S1, R2, T2, S-I, RB, TB, CG, and their primed mirrors)
values.linked_by: position (column = pipeline cycle, row = tree level) and colour (green/orange/pink band per level)
values.result_cells: no numeric result; CG marks the single cell where the memory access itself occurs

content.key_idea: One Fat-Tree QRAM query's address-routing gates (load, rotate, two-qubit gate, alternating SWAP-I/SWAP-II) are scheduled cycle by cycle down to a single controlled-gate memory access and back, and three such queries are staggered to pipeline the whole tree.
content.reading_order: left to right across pipeline cycles through the unprimed load/store/rotate/gate labels down to the CG cell at centre, then back out through the mirrored primed labels; the small tree at far left keys each row band to a QRAM level, and the bars below repeat the pattern staggered for three queries

style.stroke: thin (~0.3pt) grey grid lines with darker grey cell borders; dashed grey rules mark tree-level boundaries
style.arrows: none; the schedule's order is conveyed by column position and connecting trapezoid shading, not arrowheads
style.icons: none beyond the small line-and-circle QRAM tree reference diagram

encoding.color_means: green/orange/pink band the grid cells and tree nodes by QRAM tree level, from the bus root down to the memory cells
encoding.line_style_means: solid lines separate cells and pipeline cycles; dashed horizontal rules mark boundaries between QRAM tree levels, matching the dashed lines drawn across the reference tree
encoding.state_means: primed vs unprimed operation labels (e.g. T3 vs T'3) distinguish the query's inward descent from its mirrored outward ascent through the same tree levels
encoding.marker_means: each cell's letter code names an elementary operation (L=load, S=store, R=rotate, T=two-qubit gate, S-I/S-II=the two local-swap types, CG=the controlled gate at the memory cell); the trailing digit or B names which address qubit or the bus is acted on
encoding.emphasis: grey vertical swap-cycle bands recur at regular intervals, breaking the schedule into repeating pipeline intervals; the three staggered bars beneath the grid make the pipelining across three queries explicit
reusable_patterns: a coloured grid keyed to a small reference tree diagram, one colour per hierarchy level
trapezoidal shading linking a wide detailed table to narrow staggered summary bars repeating the same pattern over time
primed vs unprimed labels marking an outward mirror of an inward operation sequence
weaknesses: the CG operation is not defined in the quoted text, only inferred from its position at the tree's deepest level
very small (5.5pt) dense cell labels make the exact schedule hard to read without the appendix instruction-set reference

evidence: A step-by-step pipelining diagram for three capacity-8 queries using the instruction set defined in Sec. A.1.
A detailed breakdown with elementary operations appears in Appendix Fig. 12.
Alternating SWAP-I and SWAP-II enables seamless query movement across QRAM sizes

summary: This appendix figure gives the gate-level schedule behind Fat-Tree QRAM's pipelined query procedure, whose overview appears in Fig. 6 and Algorithm 1. A small reference tree at left keys three colour bands (green, orange, pink) to the QRAM's bus and two internal address levels. The main grid lays pipeline cycles out as columns and, cycle by cycle, names the elementary gate applied at each level: load (L), store (S), rotate (R), and two-qubit (T) operations on address qubits 1-3 or the bus (B), separated by alternating SWAP-I/SWAP-II local-swap cycles. Labels descend from the outer levels to a single controlled gate (CG) at the memory cell, then retrace the same path outward as mirrored, primed operations. The three narrow bars beneath repeat this coloured pattern staggered in time, showing how three capacity-8 queries share the pipeline concurrently.
